title: Issue using func.current_date() in relationship primaryjoin

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

body:
**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->
When using `func.current_date()` in a `relationship` `primaryjoin`, accessing that field after loading the object from the database emits an incorrect query that doesn't properly translate `func.current_date()`.

This issue doesn't occur with `sqlalchemy 1.3.23` and so this seems to be a regression.

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
`func.current_date()` is properly translated (to `CURRENT_DATE` in this case specifically) and the relationship field can be accessed.

**To Reproduce**

```py
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, ForeignKey, Date, MetaData, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, scoped_session, sessionmaker, selectinload

metadata = MetaData()
Base = declarative_base(metadata=metadata)


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    _date = Column(Date)
    b_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("b.id"))
    b = relationship("B")


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = "b"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_s = relationship(
        "A",
        primaryjoin="and_(B.id == A.b_id, A._date >= func.current_date())",
        viewonly=True
    )


Session = scoped_session(sessionmaker())
engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", echo=True)
Base.metadata.bind = engine
Session.configure(bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all()

Session.add(B(id=1))
Session.commit()

print(Session.query(B).options(selectinload(B.a_s)).get(1).a_s)  # works
print(Session.query(B).get(1).a_s)  # doesn't work
```

 - Python: 3.9.1

 - Database: SQLite 3

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. -->
Loading the same object with the `selectinload` eager loading option does not have this issue, and translates the query properly.
